items.title: J&K court issues notice to tehsildar over unauthorised use of beacon light on official vehicle
items.summary: A court in Kashmir has issued a show-cause notice to a tehsildar asking him to explain why appropriate legal action should not be initiated against him over unauthorised use of a red beacon/warning light and multiple-toned siren on his official vehicle. Special Mobile Magistrate (Traffic) Shabir Ahmad Malik passed the order on an application filed by one Muzaffar Ahmad through advocates Sajad Mohi-ud-din and Haroon Rashid. After examining the application and examining the material placed on record, the Court observed that a prima facie case was made out warranting an inquiry into the factual position. The Court directed SSP Traffic Rural Kashmir to physically inspect the official vehicle belonging to tehsildar Tariq Ahmad Sheikh and ascertain whether his vehicle is fitted with a red/blue beacon light and/or multi-toned siren. The Court further directed that if an unauthorised beacon or multiple-toned siren is found, the inspecting authority shall immediately seize/remove the same and initiate action under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and other relevant law. items.title: Karnataka High Court stays proceedings against man accused of ghosting, seen-zoning his partner
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently stayed criminal proceedings against a man accused of sex on the false promise of marriage after ghosting and 'seen-zoning' his partner [Thufail Ahmed v. State] . Justice M Nagaprasanna observed that the petitioner's conduct did not fulfil the ingredients of Section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. "It is the allegation that the petitioner had begun to seenzone the respondent and ghost her throughout. Therefore, the offence under s.69 has sprung. Except this there is nothing else that could become the ingredients of the offence under s.69. In that light there shall be an interim order of stay on further proceedings qua the petitioner till the next date of hearing." Justice M Nagaprasanna Both parties were in a relationship since December 2025. The petitioner told his then partner that he was visiting Chennai, where ailing father was undergoing treatment. The ex-partner, suspecting that the petitioner had told her a lie, asked him to receive her video call. The petitioner refused to receive calls and eventually blocked her. The woman then filed a complaint alleging that the petitioner had committed offences of Section 69 and 115, BNS .

Tejpal's appeal was listed before Justice Alok Aradhe today, in the chamber list in which matters are sometimes taken up for preliminary or procedural considerations before it is listed before a regular Bench. Justice Alok Aradhe Representing the Goa government, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta submitted, "Existence of the appeal is dependent on either filing a certificate that he has surrendered or, alternatively, he will have to pray to Your Lordships to allow an exemption from surrendering. These are the two options. My respectful submission is, look at the seriousness of the matter." Tushar Mehta Representing Tejpal, Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal countered that there was no need to surrender yet since the High Court itself had granted Tejpal time to surrender. "This rule doesn’t apply because this is a case where stay has been granted by the High Court, so there is no question of applying this rule. items.title: Supreme Court stays BCI order debarring former judicial officer from legal practice
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday stayed a Bar Council of India (BCI) order permanently debarring a Madhya Pradesh-based advocate, Narendra Kumar Jain from practising law. Jain had earlier served as a judicial officer before resigning from the post [ Narendra Kumar Jain v. Bar Council of India ]. The BCI had passed an order in July, debarring Jain from practice over allegations of professional misconduct arising from repeated, persistent, and unprovoked public attacks on the judiciary and individual judges. This order has now been challenged by Jain before the Supreme Court. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta today sought the BCI's response to Jain's plea and stayed the debarrment order for now. "Issue notice. In the meantime effect and operation of the impugned order will remain stayed," the Court said. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta According to a TOI report , Jain had earlier run into trouble for making comments against former Madhya Pradesh High Court Chief Justice Ravi Malimath. items.title: Sex between spouses after separation does not condone matrimonial cruelty: Calcutta High Court
items.summary: Stray instances of sexual intercourse between spouses after their separation do not, by themselves, establish that earlier acts of matrimonial cruelty were condoned, the Calcutta High Court recently held. A Division Bench of Justices Sabyasachi Bhattacharyya and Supratim Bhattacharya made the observation while upholding a decree of divorce granted to a husband on the ground of mental cruelty. The Court said, “ Stray instances of sexual intercourse after separation cannot tantamount to condonation of cruelty per se .” The couple married under the Special Marriage Act on June 18, 2009 and had a child in April 2013. They separated in 2014 after matrimonial disputes arose. The husband subsequently approached a family court seeking divorce on the ground of mental cruelty. The husband alleged that the wife repeatedly made false accusations against him and his family, filed criminal complaints and insisted that he live separately from his dependent widowed mother. In December 2021, the family court granted him a divorce, prompting the wife to appeal before the Calcutta High Court. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday asked Tamil Nadu government to approach the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) with its grievance that Karnataka was not releasing the State’s proportionate share of Cauvery water. A Bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta was hearing the Tamil Nadu government's plea seeking directions to Karnataka for immediate release of its due share of water. Appearing for Tamil Nadu, the counsel submitted, "We have to receive proportionate quantity or water, that is unfortunately not happening." The Court noted that it had previously observed that Tamil Nadu appeared to have received more water than its allocated share from Karnataka. Today, it pointed out that the State had already received water in accordance with the CWMA's directions. “You have already received the water as directed by CWMA,” said the Court. However, the counsel for Tamil Nadu contended that the CWMA had not directed the release of the proportionate quantity of water that the State was required to receive. items.title: Supreme Court bans construction activities within 100 meters of Rajasthan's Jojari River
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday banned all construction and development activities within 100 metres from the edge of Rajasthan's Jojari River till the conclusion of scientific determination and demarcation of the high flood line and ecological buffer zones [ In Re: 2 Million Lives At Risk, Contamination In Jojari River, Rajasthan ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta passed the order in a suo motu case concerning industrial pollution of rivers in Rajasthan, including the Jojari River. " We are of the considered view that it is necessary to put in place an interim, definite and measurable area of protection so as to adequately safeguard the riverine ecosystem during the pendency of the scientific exercise for the determination and demarcation of the high flood line and the requisite ecological buffer zones. Hence, we hereby direct that no construction or development activity of any nature whatsoever shall be permitted within a distance of 100 meters from the edge of the river in accordance with the aforesaid guidelines," the Court ordered.
